prompt: Match each standard library module to what it is for.
explain: These four cover most of what a beginner reaches for, and all of them ship with Python — nothing to install.

prompt: Match each import line to what it makes available.
right: sqrt(9), and every other name at once
explain: Only the plain import keeps the module name in front. The star import is the one to avoid: you can no longer tell where a name came from.

prompt: Which statements about a virtual environment are true?
choices: It keeps one project's packages separate from another's
It has to be activated before pip installs into it
It is uploaded to GitHub with your code
It makes your program run faster
explain: A virtual environment is a folder of installed packages, and it is rebuilt from requirements.txt rather than committed.

prompt: Complete the guard that stops this code running on import.
explain: __name__ is "__main__" only when the file is run directly, so the guard keeps main() from firing when another file imports this one.

prompt: Put these lines in the order they belong in a Python file.
explain: Imports go at the top, the definition next, and the call last — a function cannot be called on a line above the one that defines it.
